what: Notices, a page for one batch, and the nearest batch of a match's courses (BL-20.4, BL-20.2 and BL-20.3 completed)
method: Built-in browser on the dev API, worker and web server: a seller, a delivering organisation, two batches (one starting in two days, one with two seats), three learners; the starting sweep run for real, the full notice raised by the centre enrolling two learners; the waiting learner's notices page and the batch page opened from its link, 360 px, root font 100% and 200%, Hindi. First-load bytes from `npm run build:e2e` + `route-bundle-stats.json`. Phone bundle from `make check-mobile-budget`.

browser.notices_page_as_a_waiting_learner: two unread notices in English: 'starts on Nov 14, 2026. Ask the centre whether there is a seat for you.' and 'is now full.', each with an Open link

batch_page_hindi_360px.note: opened from the notice's own link; shows 24 of 25 seats left (one enrolled)

browser.not_checked_in_the_browser: the nearest batch inside a match's details and 'why not me' (needs a job, a gap and a course that closes it): covered by component tests only

found_by_running_it: the first version of the nearest-batches block was imported statically by SuggestedCourses and put about 7 KB on /matches and /applications (found by the budget script): it is a lazy chunk now, with a source test

first_load_bytes.note: /matches and /applications were 666,629 and 663,643 before the block became a lazy chunk

phone_bundle_bytes.note: grew 1,779 B from the new words in the three catalogues (the phone carries the web's messages whole). Sprint 102's screens come out of 19,232 B: sync only the namespaces the phone uses, or raise the ceiling.

tests.survivors: two backend survivors closed (an attended move telling again on a one-seat batch, a withdrawn learner told it is full); three web survivors closed (a far batch's warning tone, the match screen not asking, a notice's date read in a zone west of Greenwich)
